name: controlled_temporal_events
observations: The exact same deterministic perturbation vector is injected for every event.
The perturbation vector has identical norm across all event checkpoints.
Only the temporal positions of the perturbations differ between A, B, C, and D.
All temporal event checkpoints form a substantially tighter cluster in exp_avg space than their distances from the normal checkpoint.
Pairwise exp_avg distances between event classes are consistently measurable.
The model weights also retain information about the events, so optimizer state cannot be described as the only surviving channel.
The controlled experiment removes the natural-gradient variation that limited EXP-006.
exp_avg therefore provides a measurable training-history channel controlled by event timing.
conclusion: A fixed deterministic perturbation injected at different training times produces distinct and persistent Adam optimizer-state fingerprints.
The result supports using optimizer-state dynamics as the information-bearing mechanism for the CTF.
The final challenge should treat model weights as a potentially informative decoy rather than claiming that weights contain no information.
The final encoding should use a larger temporal codebook and require reconstruction of training-event timing from optimizer state.
decision: Stop mechanism experiments and proceed to the end-to-end CTF prototype using optimizer-state temporal encoding.
